steps.content: Starting with a Random Forest model using default parameters will provide a baseline for further tuning.

The Random Forest model with 100 estimators achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.96481 and a validation accuracy of 0.94737. This is a strong baseline but shows room for improvement. I'll continue experimenting with different configurations.
Increasing the number of estimators and adding a maximum depth constraint may improve the model's performance and stability.

The Random Forest model with 200 estimators and a maximum depth of 10 produced a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978, which is lower than the previous configuration. Validation accuracy remained the same at 0.94737. This configuration does not provide an improvement, so I will continue experimenting.
Testing a higher minimum samples leaf size may help reduce overfitting and improve generalization.

The Random Forest model with a minimum samples leaf size of 5 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95728 and a validation accuracy of 0.94152. Both metrics are lower than the previous best results, indicating this configuration is not beneficial. I will continue experimenting.
Exploring a configuration with fewer estimators and a maximum depth could help balance bias and variance, potentially improving accuracy.

The Random Forest model with 50 estimators and a maximum depth of 5 yielded a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95728, the same as the previous configuration, while the validation accuracy remained at 0.94737. Since this does not improve upon the best results, I will continue experimenting.
Testing a higher number of estimators along with a constrained maximum depth may help improve the model's accuracy without overfitting.

The Random Forest model with 300 estimators and a maximum depth of 10 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978, which matches a previous configuration but does not exceed it. The validation accuracy remains at 0.94737. Since there is no improvement, I will stop experimenting with Random Forest and consider switching to Gradient Boosting.

steps.final_recommendation: Consider using Gradient Boosting with a starting configuration of n_estimators=100 and learning_rate=0.1 for further exploration.
